# Iteration 2 {.unnumbered}

In Iteration 1, building the models was quick, because the raw data had already been turned into the clean starter dataset: one row per molecule, with the features and the targets in columns. In this iteration you do that work yourself. You start from the raw HOPV files of 350 molecules and turn them into a dataset in the same form as the starter dataset, with what you learned about data preparation and data understanding in Self-study Theme 2. Then you train your Iteration 1 models on it as a baseline.

A well-known saying in computing is "garbage in, garbage out": a model can only be as good as the data it learns from. If the data contains errors, if missing values are handled carelessly, or if the features don't describe the molecules well, the model learns from those problems, and a better algorithm does not fix that. This is why the data stages get a whole iteration.

The work is still structured: notebooks and resources will guide you through the main steps. However, you will begin making more decisions yourself and applying concepts introduced in the self-study material.

## Keep iterating

Although the notebooks provide a structured path, the machine-learning workflow is not strictly linear.

What you discover in the baseline may give you a reason to return to the data, change its preparation, investigate a new feature, or revisit your understanding of the problem.

In [Iteration 3](../iteration-3/index.qmd), you improve the models with cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning, take a closer look at the clusters, and score your models on the test molecules for the first time.
